newsitem.title: USA: Former football star jailed for 40 years.
newsitem.headline: Former football star jailed for 40 years.

text.p: Former National Football League star Darryl Henley was sentenced Monday to more than 40 years in prison for drug trafficking and conspiracy to murder a judge and the cheerleader who testified against him.

Henley, who had excelled as a cornerback with the Los Angeles Rams, was sentenced on the same day by two federal judges in Los Angeles after previously pleading guilty to conspiracy to murder and being found guilty of drug trafficking.

Prosecutors said Henley's targets in the murder-for-hire scheme were ex-Rams cheerleader Tracy Donaho, who testified in the drug trafficking trial that she had dated the football star and had transported cocaine across the country for him, and U.S. District Judge Gary Taylor, who presided over that trial.
According to prosecutors, Henley conspired to have the two murdered while being held in jail. The killings never took place.

U.S. District Court Judge Manual Real sentenced Henley to 260 months -- just over 21 1/2 years -- in jail on the drug charges, telling him, "You really screwed up your life, didn't you." Henley replied "Yes sir."

In another court, Federal Judge James Ideman sentenced Henley, 30, to 235 months -- or just over 19 1/2 years -- on the murder conspiracy charges, recommending that he serve his time in the U.S. penitentiary in Marion, Illinois, one of the nation's highest security facilities.
"If ever there was a guy who needs to be locked down 24 hours a day, it's Henley," Ideman said.
